course_name_en: Refrigeration, Air Conditioning and Heat Pump Technology 1
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of thermodynamics and fluid mechanics
Understanding of fundamental thermodynamic and fluid mechanical principles and laws

learning_outcomes.text: Students acquire a profound understanding of thermodynamic processes and heat transfer in refrigeration and heat pump systems as well as associated storage systems.
The physical principles, components, and functionalities are conveyed through subject matter delivery, own calculations, and accompanying laboratory experiments.
Students design, calculate, and analyze processes and systems in this context.
They independently solve concrete problems and critically question the application and significance of the technologies.

syllabus_topics: Refrigerants and their environmental impacts (local and global)
Refrigeration systems based on the vapor-compression principle
Heat pumps based on the vapor-compression principle
Components of refrigeration systems and heat pumps
Classification of thermal storage according to physical principles
Fields of application and motivation for application
Thermodynamic principles: operating principles, material data and heat transfer
Sensible heat storage with water and solid storage media
Latent heat storage: phase change materials and ice storage systems
Integration and operating strategies of thermal storage in system technology

assessment_methods.method: Written examination/exam (120 min) as module examination
Ungraded study performance: laboratory reports for MABB441D
